stem.text: The function g is differentiable for all real numbers, and selected values of g and its derivative are given in the table. Find \( \lim_{x \to 5} \left(3 g(x) + 1\right) \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: The limit is -26, because g is differentiable at \( x = 5 \), so it is continuous there, and \( \lim_{x \to 5} g(x) = g(5) = -9 \).

worked_solution.text: g is differentiable at \( x = 5 \), so it is continuous there.
By the limit laws the limit is 3(-9) + 1 = -26.
worked_solution.rule_named: sum and constant multiple limit laws

options.label: The limit is -26, because every function has its limit equal to its value at each input, and \( \lim_{x \to 5} g(x) = g(5) = -9 \).
options.derivation: the conclusion used as if it held for every function, with no hypothesis about g checked

options.label: The limit is -26, because the table gives a value of g at every listed input, so g is continuous at \( x = 5 \), and \( \lim_{x \to 5} g(x) = g(5) = -9 \).
